fixes.explanation: The word is "assist." God says the Levites will join Aaron and assist him and his sons before the Tent of the Testimony. They're the helpers, and God Himself picked them for the job. Every good bakery needs the people who make the whole morning run.

That's the line. God says the Levites "…must not come near to the furnishings of the sanctuary or the altar, or both they and you will die." The Levites have plenty to do around the Tent, but those two things are off limits to them. Notice the "you" there too, because Aaron is part of what's at stake.

Right on the money, baker. God says the purpose of Aaron's duties at the sanctuary and the altar is that wrath not fall on the Israelites a second time. That "again" is a heavy word. I think it points back to what the Israelites just went through, and it tells me this job matters a great deal.

The word is "gift." God says He selected the Levites "…as a gift to you, dedicated to the LORD…" Aaron gets a whole crew of helpers handed to him, and they're set apart for the service of the Tent of Meeting. I got a quarter-store price sticker and a drawer. Aaron got a team. I'm only a little jealous.

God says, “…any outsider who comes near the sanctuary must be put to death.” This one is heavy. Right before it, God says only Aaron and his sons shall attend to the priesthood, everything concerning the altar and what is inside the veil. That work is theirs, and God gives it to them as a gift.

God tells Aaron, “I am your portion and your inheritance among the Israelites.” Aaron gets no inheritance in their land and no portion among them. What he gets is God Himself. I think that's the best inheritance in the whole passage.

The firstborn do show up earlier, but they're not the Levites' inheritance. God says the firstborn offered to the LORD belong to Aaron, though every firstborn son and every firstborn male of unclean animals must be redeemed (Numbers 18:15). For the Levites, God's word is "tithes." He gives them all the tithes in Israel as an inheritance for their work at the Tent of Meeting.
God says, “No longer may the Israelites come near to the Tent of Meeting, or they will incur guilt and die.” That's a heavy line. The work at the Tent belongs to the Levites and the priests.

Losing land isn't the consequence God names. The Levites are the ones with no land among the Israelites, because God gave them the tithe as their inheritance. For Israelites who come near the Tent, God says the result is guilt and death.

Being sent out of the camp isn't in this verse. God says that Israelites who come near the Tent of Meeting will bring guilt on themselves and die. That's a heavy line, and the verse gives no other consequence.

God says, “…from these you are to give the LORD’s offering to Aaron the priest.” The Israelites give the tithe to the Levites, and then the Levites present part of what they receive to Aaron. So Aaron is the one who receives the LORD's offering.
Smallest? That's the broken cookie hiding at the bottom of the box, friend. God says the offering comes from "…all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it." The word is "best."

Oldest? That's the batch that's been sitting on the counter since last Tuesday. Nobody wants to hand that over. God says the offering comes from "…all the best of every gift, the holiest part of it." The word is "best."

The passage ends with a heavy line: “But you must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, or else you will die.” The Levites have been given a big job, and the sacred offerings are to be treated as sacred. I think that's a weighty way to end.
There's no fine in this verse. God says the Levites must not defile the sacred offerings of the Israelites, "…or else you will die." It's a serious closing line, and the text states it plainly.
